arxiv-2101-11003.title: FDApy : a Python package for functional data
arxiv-2101-11003.creator: Steven Golovkine
arxiv-2101-11003.description: Abstract We introduce FDApy , an open-source Python package for the analysis of functional data. The package provides tools for the representation of (multivariate) functional data defined on different dimensional domains and for functional data that is irregularly sampled. Additionally, dimension reduction techniques are implemented for multivariate and/or multidimensional functional data that are regularly or irregularly sampled.

arxiv-2108-13765.title: Triple-Structured Compressive Sensing-based Channel Estimation for RIS-aided MU-MIMO Systems
arxiv-2108-13765.description: Abstract Reconfigurable intelligent surface (RIS) has been recognized as a potential technology for 5G beyond and attracted tremendous research attention. However, channel estimation in RIS-aided system is still a critical challenge due to the excessive amount of parameters in cascaded channel. The existing compressive sensing (CS)-based RIS estimation schemes only adopt incomplete sparsity, which induces redundant pilot consumption.

arxiv-2111-07968.title: On the spine of the two-particle Fleming-Viot process driven by Brownian motion
arxiv-2111-07968.creator: Krzysztof Burdzy, Tvrtko Tadić
arxiv-2111-07968.description: Abstract The spine of the two-particle Fleming-Viot process driven by Brownian motion is not a Bessel-3 process. keywords Fleming-Viot type process ; Brownian motion ; Bessel process ; logarithmic transformation AMS 60G17 ; 60J65 ; 60J80 † † shorttitle: Spine of Fleming-Viot process † † support: Supported in part by Simons Foundation Grant 506732. † † email: burdzy@uw.

arxiv-2204-00915.title: Optical computing of quantum revivals
arxiv-2204-00915.creator: M. R. Maia, D. Jonathan, T. R. de Oliveira, A. Z. Khoury, D. S. Tasca
arxiv-2204-00915.description: Abstract Interference is the mechanism through which waves can be structured into the most fascinating patterns. While for sensing, imaging, trapping, or in fundamental investigations, structured waves play nowadays an important role and are becoming subject of many interesting studies.

arxiv-2309-06540.title: Identifying Bayesian Optimal Experiments for Uncertain Biochemical Pathway Models
arxiv-2309-06540.creator: Natalie M. Isenberg, Susan D. Mertins, Byung-Jun Yoon, Kristofer Reyes, Nathan M. Urban
arxiv-2309-06540.description: Abstract Summary Pharmacodynamic (PD) models are mathematical models of cellular reaction networks that include drug mechanisms of action. These models are useful for studying predictive therapeutic outcomes of novel drug therapies in silico . However, PD models are known to possess significant uncertainty with respect to constituent parameter data, leading to uncertainty in the model predictions.

arxiv-2312-10345.title: Multi-Target Two-way Integrated Sensing and Communications with Full Duplex MIMO Radios
arxiv-2312-10345.creator: Muhammad Talha 1 , Besma Smida 1 , Md Atiqul Islam 2 , and George C. Alexandropoulos 3
arxiv-2312-10345.description: Abstract In this paper, we propose a multiple input multiple output (MIMO) Full-Duplex Integrated Sensing and Communication System consisting of multiple targets, a single downlink, and a single uplink user. We employed signal-to-interference plus noise ratio (SINR) as the performance metric for radar, downlink, and uplink communication.

arxiv-2403-13345.title: Local Approximation of Secrecy Capacity
arxiv-2403-13345.creator: Emmanouil M. Athanasakos 1 , Nicholas Kalouptsidis 2 and Hariprasad Manjunath 1
arxiv-2403-13345.description: Abstract This paper uses Euclidean Information Theory (EIT) to analyze the wiretap channel. We investigate a scenario of efficiently transmitting a small amount of information subject to compression rate and secrecy constraints. We transform the information-theoretic problem into a linear algebra problem and obtain the perturbed probability distributions such that secrecy is achievable.

arxiv-2404-02591.title: Adaptive Sampling Policies Imply Biased Beliefs: A Generalization of the Hot Stove Effect
arxiv-2404-02591.creator: Jerker Denrell University of Warwick jdenrell@gmail.com
arxiv-2404-02591.description: Abstract . The Hot Stove Effect is a negativity bias resulting from the adaptive character of learning. The mechanism is that learning algorithms that pursue alternatives with positive estimated values, but avoid alternatives with negative estimated values, will correct errors of overestimation but fail to correct errors of underestimation.

arxiv-2407-03700.title: Deep learning architectures for data-driven damage detection in nonlinear dynamic systems
arxiv-2407-03700.creator: Harrish Joseph, Giuseppe Quaranta, Biagio Carboni, Walter Lacarbonara
arxiv-2407-03700.description: Abstract The primary goal of structural health monitoring is to detect damage at its onset before it reaches a critical level. The in-depth investigation in the present work addresses deep learning applied to data-driven damage detection in nonlinear dynamic systems. In particular, autoencoders (AEs) and generative adversarial networks (GANs) are implemented leveraging on 1D convolutional neural networks.

arxiv-2411-02672.title: Multi-modal deformable image registration using untrained neural networks
arxiv-2411-02672.creator: Quang Luong Nhat Nguyen, Ruiming Cao, Laura Waller
arxiv-2411-02672.description: Abstract Image registration techniques usually assume that the images to be registered are of a certain type (e.g. single- vs. multi-modal, 2D vs. 3D, rigid vs. deformable) and there lacks a general method that can work for data under all conditions. We propose a registration method that utilizes neural networks for image representation.

arxiv-2501-05943.title: Koopman-Based Model Predictive Control of Functional Electrical Stimulation for Ankle Dorsiflexion and Plantarflexion Assistance
arxiv-2501-05943.creator: Mayank Singh, Noor Hakam, Trisha M. Kesar, Nitin Sharma*
arxiv-2501-05943.description:
A 2025 arXiv research paper by Mayank Singh, Noor Hakam, Trisha M. Kesar, Nitin Sharma*. Functional Electrical Stimulation (FES)
can be an effective tool to augment paretic muscle function and restore
normal ankle function. Our approach incorporates a real-time, data-driven
Model Predictive Control (MPC) scheme, built upon a Koopman operator
theory (KOT) framework. This framework adeptly captures the complex
nonlinear dynamics of ankle motion in a linearized form, enabling
application of linear control approaches for highly-nonlinear FES-actuated
dynamics.

pmc-10573628.creator: Paweł Bańka, Maciej Wybraniec, Tomasz Bochenek, Bartosz Gruchlik, Aleksandra Burchacka, Andrzej Swinarew, Katarzyna Mizia-Stec
pmc-10573628.description: Aortic valve stenosis (AS) is a common heart valve disease in the elderly population, and its pathogenesis remains an interesting area of research. The degeneration of the aortic valve leaflets gradually progresses to valve sclerosis. The advanced phase is marked by the presence of extracellular fibrosis and calcification.

pmc-12777079.title: Conceptualized Immersive Projection Environment (CIPE-NRT©): A Novel Immersive Projection Environment for Multisensory Modulation in Pediatric Dental Anxiety Management
pmc-12777079.creator: Nilesh Rathi, Swagata Saha
pmc-12777079.description: Pediatric dental anxiety continues to present a significant barrier to effective oral healthcare delivery, often necessitating pharmacological interventions or rudimentary distraction techniques. Although audiovisual (AV) aids have found widespread application in dental behavior management, their limited sensory scope often fails to create a transformative experience.

pmc-13009373.title: Cross-cancer survival prediction using machine learning models
pmc-13009373.creator: Lucas Buk Cardoso, Jones Eduardo Egydio, Tatiana Natasha Toporcov, Nanci Yumi Utida, Maria Paula Curado, Gisele Aparecida Fernandes, Adeylson Guimarães Ribeiro, Bryan Gilvaz Chin, Vanderlei Cunha Parro
pmc-13009373.description: Among the many challenges faced by healthcare systems, cancer remains one of the most urgent. This makes the application of artificial intelligence a critical tool for enhancing early detection and optimizing treatment strategies, especially given the growing volume of patient data being collected.

pmc-13181877.title: Metabolic targeting of pantothenate by medium chain fats in glioblastoma cells
pmc-13181877.creator: Erwann Pain, Pankaj K Singh, Yasin Khan, George Mears, Xiaoping Yang, Steven Lynham, Paul F. Devlin, Tricia Rutherford, Katie Lloyd Jones, Matthew C. Walker, Philip Beesley, Matthew S. Gentry, Robin SB Williams
pmc-13181877.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Ketogenic diets are commonly used for epilepsy therapy and are increasingly being considered in cancer treatment, where metabolic reprogramming triggered by glucose restriction and ketosis alters energy provision as the therapeutic mechanism. However, a recently developed medium chain triglyceride product, with a high decanoic acid (DA) to octanoic acid (OA) ratio (DA: OA) has enabled a much less restrictive diet and is clinically effective as an epilepsy treatment, yet no studies have explored the product in cancer models.

pmc-13280839.title: Development of a Tannic Acid-Gelatin Modified Filter Paper Membrane for Trace Lead Detection in Water
pmc-13280839.creator: Arinrada Rattanadechawan, Nathawut Choengchan, Thitirat Mantim, Suchao Donpudsa, Chanpen Karuwan, Nuanlaor Ratanawimarnwong
pmc-13280839.description: A novel membrane-based solid-phase extraction (SPE) device was developed using cellulose filter paper modified with a tannic acid–gelatin (TA/GE) composite for the preconcentration of lead (Pb­(II)) ions from aqueous samples. The TA/GE sorbent layer was fabricated via cross-linking gelatin with tannic acid at pH 9, forming a stable, partially insoluble network that enhances the membrane’s mechanical strength and ion-binding capability.

pmc-13465072.title: Diagnostic value of piezogenic papules in childhood: A scoping review and analysis of existing data
pmc-13465072.creator: Elke Schubert-Hjalmarsson, Ann-Charlott Söderpalm
pmc-13465072.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). IntroductionPiezogenic papules (PP) are soft, skin-colored or yellowish herniations of subcutaneous fat appearing under pressure, commonly on the heels. While usually benign, they may cause pain and have been associated with Ehlers-Danlos syndrome.

uslaw-usc-t10-s2273a.title: 10 U.S.C. § 2273a — Space Rapid Capabilities Office
uslaw-usc-t10-s2273a.creator: United States Congress
uslaw-usc-t10-s2273a.description: United States Code, Title 10 (Armed Forces); Part IV (Service, Supply, And Property); Chapter 135 (Space Programs). Current through Public Law 119-134, as published by the Office of the Law Revision Counsel. (a) In General.— There is within the Space Force a program office known as the Space Rapid Capabilities Office (in this section referred to as the “Office”). The facilities of the Office may not be co-located with the headquarters facilities.
